opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new data-infrastructure chips and platforms; up 3% YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling the chips and running the company; down 6% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring related charges
opex.note: Severance and facilities charges from the ongoing restructuring; down from $42.0M a year ago.

footerNote: Marvell guided Q3 FY25 revenue to $1.450B ±5% — 14% sequential growth at the midpoint, with every end market growing.
oneTimers: GAAP results include $154.9M of stock-based compensation and $275.7M of amortization of acquired intangible assets, both excluded from non-GAAP — that is why non-GAAP net income ($266.2M) is $459.5M above the GAAP net loss (-$193.3M).
Restructuring-related charges were $4.0M this quarter, down from $42.0M a year ago; the big restructuring and impairment charges hit in earlier quarters.
Marvell recorded a $47.1M tax provision despite a $146.2M pre-tax loss — the tax line adds to the loss rather than softening it, unlike a year ago when it was a $44.1M benefit.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $48.4M, partly offset by $2.6M of interest income and other, net, makes up the $45.8M outside operations.
pngFooterNote: Marvell guided Q3 FY25 revenue to $1.45B ±5%.

segments.name: Data center
segments.note: Chips for AI data centers — custom silicon, optics and Ethernet switches; 69% of all revenue.

segments.name: Enterprise networking
segments.note: Campus and small-business routers, switches and wireless access points; 12% of revenue.

segments.name: Carrier infrastructure
segments.note: Broadband access, optical transport and wireless radio gear for carriers; 6% of revenue.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: Broadband gateways, gaming consoles, home storage and PCs; 7% of revenue.

segments.name: Automotive/industrial
segments.note: Driver-assistance, in-vehicle networking and industrial Ethernet; 6% of revenue.

takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit $880.9M — 69% of the company — up 92% YoY as electro-optics products grew and custom AI programs began to ramp, and total revenue grew 10% sequentially, above the midpoint of guidance.
takeaways.title: Data Center nearly doubled

takeaways.text: GAAP net loss was $193.3M, or -$0.22 per share, versus a $207.5M loss a year ago. Operating loss was $100.4M, as R&D and SG&A alone ($684.0M) exceeded gross profit of $587.6M — but non-GAAP net income was $266.2M, or $0.30 per share.
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss

takeaways.text: Marvell guided Q3 FY25 revenue to $1.450B ±5% — 14% sequential growth at the midpoint — with all five end markets growing sequentially and enterprise networking and carrier returning to growth, plus a big jump in operating leverage.
takeaways.title: Every market expected to grow next quarter

verdict: Marvell's AI data-center sales nearly doubled, but the rest of the business shrank so much that total revenue fell 5% — and on a GAAP basis the company still lost $193M.
